# Before you sign up for another API

When a task needs outside data and the user has not named a provider, do this before you suggest creating an account or an API key:

1. Say the task in 3 to 8 plain words, for example "find a work email" or "Google search results for a keyword".
2. Run `python3 .claude/skills/before-you-sign-up/looot_price.py "<task>"`. It reads looot's free public catalog with one GET. It needs no token and spends nothing.
3. Show the table the script prints. Then say in two or three sentences: the cheapest and dearest price per call, and that one call is not always the same product at every provider.
4. Say plainly that this is looot's catalog and that prices are looot list prices, not each vendor's own page. Give the user the choice. Signing up with a provider directly is a normal option, and looot is one option. Do not push either.
5. Do not call looot `run`, any provider, or any paid tool. If the user wants to proceed through looot, tell them the endpoint id and stop. Spending needs their say.

Do not use this skill for tasks that need no outside data, such as editing code, explaining a concept or reading a local file.

content.text:
I checked looot's public catalog. It was a single read, so nothing ran and nothing was charged.

| Provider | Endpoint | Price | Unit | Cost for 30 sites |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| builtwith | builtwith-free1-api-json | $0 | call | $0 |
| tomba | tomba-technology | $0.0089 | call | ~$0.27 |
| predictleads | predictleads-companies-technology-detections | $0.01 | call | ~$0.30 |
| sumble | sumble-organizations-techs | $0.01 | result | depends on result count |
| builtwith | builtwith-api-json | $0.0495 | call | ~$1.49 |
| theirstack | theirstack-companies-technologies | $0.0981 | call | ~$2.94 |

Paid calls run from under a cent (tomba) to about 10 cents (theirstack), so 30 sites costs between nothing and about $3. Price isn't the main difference between them, though. BuiltWith's free tier returns only technology categories, not the actual tool names. The full BuiltWith endpoint returns specific technologies with first-seen and last-seen dates. TheirStack and Sumble work out the stack partly from job postings, which catches backend tools that never show up in a site's HTML. For a GTM list, pick the provider whose data fits what you plan to do with it, not the cheapest one.

These prices come from looot's catalog, and every row is marked unverified. They're looot's list prices, so they may not match each vendor's own pricing page. You can sign up with any of these providers directly, or go through looot. Both work.

You may not need an API at all. At 30 sites, an open-source detector run locally is free and finishes in about a minute. Examples are `httpx -tech-detect` from ProjectDiscovery or `webanalyze`, which uses the Wappalyzer fingerprints. Both only see what the public pages expose: frontend frameworks, CMS, analytics, chat widgets, CDN. They won't find your prospects' CRM or data warehouse.

Tell me which way you want to go. If it's looot, give me the endpoint id and I'll stop there so you can approve the spend. If it's the local tool, send me the 30 domains and I'll run it.
